name.en: WhatsApp group “video call code”: your account is taken over

how.en: You get a WhatsApp audio call from someone pretending to be a member of a group you are in, often with a copied name or photo. They say they are sending a one-time code so you can join a group video call, and ask you to share it. The code is really the registration code for your account. Once they have it, they lock you out with two-step verification and message your contacts asking for money.

text.en: A WhatsApp audio call comes from someone who seems to be in one of your groups.
They say they are sending you a code to join a group video call and ask you to read it out.
They take over your account and lock you out.
Your friends and family get messages from “you” asking for money urgently.
Hi, it's Sue from the group. We're doing a video call for members later. I've just sent you a 6 digit code to register you, can you send it back to me?

en: Anyone asking for a code that WhatsApp sent you.
A group member calling out of the blue about a video call.
Friends asking for money urgently over WhatsApp.
Never share a WhatsApp code with anyone, even someone you know.
Turn on two-step verification in WhatsApp settings.
Report and block the sender in WhatsApp. If money was sent, call your bank.
